The '''1995–96 Scottish Premier Division''' season was the second season involving a [[Playoffs#Scotland|relegation playoff]] with the [[Scottish First Division]]. The season began on 26 August 1995.

==Overview==
The 1995–96 Scottish Premier Division season ended in success for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who won the title by four points from nearest rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] to clinch eight titles in a row, despite Celtic losing only one league match in the entire season. [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] were relegated to the [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] after finishing bottom with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] also being relegated after losing the relegation playoff to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Celtic were joined by third-placed [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Fourth-placed [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] as [[Scottish Cup]] runners-up.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem96.htm|title=Scottish Premier Division 1995/96|publisher=Soccerbot|access-date=4 June 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080514141514/http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem96.htm| archive-date= 14 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

The season began on 26 August with the first goal of the season scored by Aberdeen's [[John Inglis (footballer, born 1966)|John Inglis]] as they won 3–2 away to Falkirk. The regular league season ended on 4 May with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s [[Darren Jackson (Scottish footballer)|Darren Jackson]] netting a late winner in a 1–0 win at home to Partick Thistle to claim the final goal of the season.

==Events==
* 14 October: [[Gordon Durie]] hits the first [[hat-trick]] of the season in a 4–0 win at [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].
* 28 April: [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] win the title at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] as a [[Paul Gascoigne]] hat-trick helps them to a 3–1 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Play-off==
A two leg play-off took place between the 9th placed team in the Premier Division (Partick Thistle) and the runner-up of the [[1995–96 Scottish First Division|First Division]] ([[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]) for a place in the [[1996–97 Scottish Premier Division]].

The first leg at [[Firhill Stadium]] finished 1–1 and the second leg at [[Tannadice Park]] four days later also finished 1–1 after 90 minutes, meaning extra time was required to separate the teams. [[Owen Coyle]] scored for Dundee United during extra time, meaning Dundee United won 3–2 on aggregate, and returned to the Premier Division and Partick Thistle were relegated to the [[1996–97 Scottish First Division|First Division]].
